items.name: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
items.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
items.description: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. items.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
items.description: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. items.name: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
items.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
items.description: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. items.name: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
items.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
items.description: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware. items.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
items.description: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. items.name: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
items.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
items.description: To interpret a direction in a language model's residual stream, we can look for text that strongly activates it. But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains. We develop Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs), language models which map residual stream directions from a subject model to text exemplars that strongly activate those directions. items.name: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
items.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
items.description: Adversarial Training (AT) is an important method for improving model robustness. We study the dynamics of deterministic Gradient Descent (GD) in AT. Most existing works in this direction focus on the small or vanishing step sizes regime, where GD resembles a continuous-time flow. However, such step sizes can make training inefficient and are rarely used in practice. In this paper, we study the AT dynamics of GD with large constant step sizes. items.name: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
items.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
items.description: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. items.name: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
items.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
items.description: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. items.title: A Hidden Markov Preference Model for Online Prediction of Adversary Actions
items.description: A defender anticipating an attacker needs a probability distribution over the attacker's next action from information available before that action occurs. Two structures complicate this: the attacker's behavioral regime persists and can switch within an episode, and each action combines an operation with state-dependent arguments whose feasible values change over time. items.title: Label-Wording Augmentation in a Typed-Decision Encoder: Gains on Unfamiliar Words, Not on Abbreviations or Codes
items.description: Typed-decision models score options that the caller supplies at request time, so their accuracy depends on label wording that the model's developer does not control. We compare two releases of a 307M-parameter multilingual cross-encoder, Ru-Jev, trained on thirteen Russian-language tasks; the later release adds an augmentation that presents labels in several surface forms. items.name: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
items.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
items.description: Neural networks are likely to be among the most consequential artefacts in human history. As these systems become more capable and autonomous, their potential to cause societal harm also grows, making AI safety one of the defining challenges of our time. items.name: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
items.title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
items.description: LLM-based medical assistants that follow a patient across visits need a memory that keeps the patient's clinical state correct as it changes. We examine the errors of five memory systems on longitudinal medical dialogue and find three recurring causes: the retrieved evidence gives an outdated state, includes another person's health facts, or lacks a safety fact the answer depends on. items.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
items.description: Chat remains the default surface for many large language model (LLM) tasks, even as agentic tools such as OpenCode excel at coding and automation. items.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
items.description: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. items.description: Molecular representations such as fingerprints and learned embeddings play a central role in cheminformatics and small-molecule machine learning. They serve as the primary input for a diverse array of tasks, including clustering, dataset splitting, and virtual screening, yet their evaluation is often limited to downstream model performance on narrow benchmark tasks. items.description: Coding agents are among the most economically consequential deployments of LLMs to date, making reliable evaluation increasingly important. Yet even benchmarks that are carefully validated at release can become stale. items.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning
items.description: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is commonly used in both supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), often under similar optimizer settings. items.title: The Gold Rush in AI4Math, II: What are signatures of AI-assisted Proofs?
items.description: The growing use of AI in mathematics raises a question: can we detect AI involvement in proofs, separately from AI assistance with writing? Historical arXiv papers, recent papers disclosing substantive AI use, and manuscripts released by OpenAI provide a rich empirical basis for studying this question. items.title: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs
items.description: Uncertainty quantification is crucial in scientific machine learning, where models inform safety-critical tasks such as flood forecasting, financial risk management, and thermal control in machines. items.name: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
items.title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
items.description: Humanoid robots are typically trained as solitary agents, leaving them unable to coordinate physically with human partners who naturally anticipate and adjust to one another. items.title: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout
